info.name: FoC Supplier Service (D2)
info.description: The Supplier Service D2 demo: query patterns, denied requests, and CRUD through the API alone. Import together with local.postman_environment.json; see api/README.md.

item.name: 0 Setup (log in)
item.description: Log in once as each demo user. Their tokens are stored in the environment (basicToken, adminToken) and sent as Authorization: Bearer by every Supplier Service request, so both users can be used side by side. Alternatively, paste tokens into the environment by hand.

request.description: Logs in at user-service and saves the access token as {{basicToken}}. The token arrives only as the httpOnly access_token cookie.
Logs in at user-service and saves the access token as {{adminToken}}. The token arrives only as the httpOnly access_token cookie.

item.name: 1 Query patterns (D2 point 2)
item.description: Any logged-in user may read (F13.3). Run as the basic user.

request.description: In-use buildings with names and coordinates (F4.4). Saves PGP and COM3 ids for later requests.
In-use categories (F11.4). Saves the Food and Coffee ids.
Paginated listing, sorted by display name then id (F5.1-F5.3, N3.1). Saves the first supplier's id.
Case-insensitive partial name match (F5.4.1).
Suppliers in a building: 'finding suppliers by location' (F5.4.3).
Suppliers with any of the given categories (F5.4.2).

exec: pm.test('all have Coffee', () => pm.response.json().items.forEach((s) => pm.expect(s.categories.map((c) => c.name)).to.include('Coffee')));

request.description: Filters combine with AND (F5.5); caller-chosen sort, id as final tie-breaker (F5.3.1).
Offset/limit paging (F5.2, N3.1).
All fields including version; the version is also the ETag (F5.9, F15.1).
A distinct not-found response (F5.9.1).
Unknown and malformed parameters are rejected, all listed at once (F5.8, N8.4.1).

item.name: 2 Denied requests (D2 points 2 and 4)
item.description: How denied requests are answered: no token → 401 (F13.2); a basic user on an admin action → 403, and nothing is changed (F13.5).

item.name: 3 CRUD as admin (D2 point 3)
item.description: Create, read, update and 'delete' (= set Inactive) through the API alone. Each run uses a fresh supplier name, so the folder can be re-run.

request.description: Admin-only direct create (F7.5): Active, version 1, with Location and ETag headers.
Same name, building and floor: rejected by the database's unique constraint (F1.5, F1.5.2).

item.name: Create with several problems (400, all listed)

request.description: Field rules, unknown references and system-managed fields are all reported in one response (F1.6.1, F1.3.2).
Any logged-in user can read it (F13.3).
An edit must state the version it is based on (F14.3).
Direct admin update of some fields (F8.6); the version goes up by 1 (F1.3.1).

exec: pm.test('fields changed', () => { pm.expect(s.locationDescription).to.eql('Opposite the lift'); pm.expect(s.categories.map((c) => c.name)).to.have.members(['Coffee', 'Food']); });

request.description: Someone else's change is not silently overwritten: conflict with the current version (F14.3.1).
Admin-only status change (F9.5). The supplier stays in the database, tagged Inactive; errands already created are unaffected (F9.6).

exec: pm.test('Inactive at version 3', () => { const s = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(s.status).to.eql('Inactive'); pm.expect(s.version).to.eql(3); });

request.description: Only Active <-> Inactive is allowed (F9.2).

item.name: Active list no longer shows it

request.description: Filtered by status Active (F5.4.5).
Inactive suppliers remain available in lookups (F5.7).

item.name: 4 Supplier requests (D2 points 3 and 4)
item.description: Moderated changes (F6, F7, F8): a basic user asks for a new supplier or an edit; an admin reviews, approves or denies; the user follows their own requests and may withdraw a pending one. Nothing changes until an admin approves.

item.name: Basic user asks to add a supplier (201, Pending)

request.description: Any logged-in user may file a request (F7.1, F13.3). It is validated exactly like an admin's create; the supplier does not exist yet.
An identical request is already Pending (F7.2), enforced by a partial unique index in the database.
Reviewing requests is admin-only (F13.4).
Pending requests, oldest first (F6.7).
Creates the supplier and records the approval in one transaction (F6.8). Duplicates are checked again at this moment (F7.3.1).

exec: pm.test('Approved, with who and when', () => { pm.expect(r.state).to.eql('Approved'); pm.expect(r.resolvedBy).to.be.ok; pm.expect(r.resolvedAt).to.be.ok; });

request.description: A request is resolved exactly once (F6.3).

item.name: Basic user asks to edit it (201, Pending)

request.description: Any logged-in user may propose an edit (F8.1), based on the version they saw (If-Match, as for an admin edit). Validated exactly like an admin PATCH.

exec: pm.test('Pending Update request on version 1', () => { pm.expect(r.type).to.eql('Update'); pm.expect(r.state).to.eql('Pending'); pm.expect(r.supplierVersion).to.eql(1); });
pm.test('only the changed field is recorded', () => pm.expect(r.values).to.eql({ locationDescription: 'Beside the vending machines, level 3 lobby' }));

item.name: Second edit for the same supplier (409)

request.description: A supplier has at most one pending edit (F8.3), enforced by a partial unique index.
F8.2: the listing keeps returning the live record until an admin approves.

exec: pm.test('still version 1, old description', () => { pm.expect(s.version).to.eql(1); pm.expect(s.locationDescription).to.eql('Beside the vending machines'); });

request.description: Applies the changes through the same code as an admin PATCH (F8.4). Refused with 409 VERSION_CONFLICT if the supplier changed since the request was filed (F8.4.1).

exec: pm.test('new description at version 2', () => { pm.expect(s.version).to.eql(2); pm.expect(s.locationDescription).to.eql('Beside the vending machines, level 3 lobby'); });

item.name: Basic user asks for another supplier

request.description: A denial needs a reason of 1-500 characters (F6.4).

exec: pm.test('Denied, with the reason', () => { pm.expect(r.state).to.eql('Denied'); pm.expect(r.denialReason).to.eql('Could not find it at COM3 level 4'); pm.expect(r.createdSupplierId).to.eql(null); });

request.description: The caller's own requests of every type and state, newest first, paged (F6.5). Filter with ?state= and ?type=.

exec: pm.test('newest first', () => { const t = page.items.map((r) => r.submittedAt); pm.expect(t).to.eql([...t].sort().reverse()); });
pm.test('includes the denial reason', () => pm.expect(byId[pm.environment.get('deniedRequestId')].denialReason).to.eql('Could not find it at COM3 level 4'));

item.name: Basic user views the denied request

request.description: One request, for its submitter or an admin. Anyone else gets 404, exactly as for an unknown id (F13.6).

exec: pm.test('Denied, with the reason', () => { const r = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(r.state).to.eql('Denied'); pm.expect(r.denialReason).to.be.a('string'); });

item.name: Basic user asks for a third supplier

request.description: Only the submitter may withdraw. To anyone else the request does not exist (F13.6); an admin rejects a request by denying it.
Withdraws the caller's own Pending request (F6.6). It leaves the admin queue, and the same request may be filed again.

item.name: Tidy up: read the approved supplier

request.description: The last two requests deactivate the demo supplier, so re-runs don't fill the Active list.

item.name: 5 Moderation: status changes, categories, buildings
item.description: Added after D2. A basic user asks for a supplier to be deactivated and an admin approves (F9.3, F9.4); an admin renames and retires a category (F11.2, F11.3) and creates, edits and retires a building (F4.3). Run folder 1 first (it saves the Food category and the COM3 building ids). Each run creates new timestamped names, so it can be re-run.

item.name: Admin creates a supplier to deactivate (201)
Basic user asks to deactivate it (201, Pending)

request.description: Any logged-in user may ask for a supplier to be deactivated or reactivated (F9.3). No If-Match: the request records the supplier's version when filed.

exec: pm.test('Pending StatusChange on version 1', () => { pm.expect(r.type).to.eql('StatusChange'); pm.expect(r.state).to.eql('Pending'); pm.expect(r.supplierVersion).to.eql(1); });
pm.test('status and reason recorded', () => pm.expect(r.values).to.eql({ status: 'Inactive', reason: 'Closed for renovation' }));

request.description: A supplier has at most one pending status change (F9.3.2), enforced by a partial unique index.

item.name: Ask for the status it already has (409)

request.description: The supplier is already Active (F9.3.1).
Applies the status in the same transaction as the approval (F9.4).

item.name: Rename to a name in use (409)

request.description: Case-insensitive (F11.2.1).
Suppliers keep it; it is no longer listed or selectable (F11.3, F11.3.1).

item.name: Retired category is no longer listed

request.description: Coordinates must lie inside the campus box (F1.2.7).
F4.3. Every name must be free among in-use buildings (F4.2).
Suppliers keep it; it is no longer listed or selectable, and its names become free (F4.3.1).

item.name: Retired building is no longer listed
6 Opening hours (after D2)
item.description: Weekly hours in Singapore time (F2): create with hours, the computed isOpenNow and nextChangeAt, validation errors with their paths, overnight and open-24-hours, editing and removing, the openNow filter, and a user proposing hours in a request. Run folder 1 first (it saves the Food category and the COM3 building ids). Names are timestamped, so it can be re-run.

item.name: Admin creates a supplier with weekly hours (201)

request.description: Weekly hours in Singapore time (F2.1): two intervals on Monday (a lunch break), Saturday morning, and no Sunday, so Sunday is closed (F2.1.2).

item.name: Read it: hours, isOpenNow and nextChangeAt (200)

request.description: isOpenNow and nextChangeAt are computed from the clock in Singapore time on every read, so they change through the day.

exec: pm.test('hours returned in canonical form, Sunday left out', () => { pm.expect(Object.keys(s.openingHours.days)).to.eql(['mon','tue','wed','thu','fri','sat']); pm.expect(s.openingHours.days.mon).to.eql([{ opens: '09:00', closes: '12:00' }, { opens: '13:00', closes: '18:00' }]); });
pm.test('isOpenNow is a boolean, worked out when asked (F2.5)', () => pm.expect(s.isOpenNow).to.be.a('boolean'));

item.name: Hours with several problems (400, every path listed)

request.description: An invalid time, equal opening and closing, and an overlap, all reported together (F2.4, F1.6.1). Nothing is saved.

item.name: Open 24 hours cannot be combined with days (400)

request.description: An edit that mentions openingHours replaces the whole schedule and bumps the version (F14.3). The Friday interval is overnight: open until 02:00 on Saturday (F2.3).

exec: pm.test('version 2, only the hours changed', () => { const r = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(r.version).to.eql(2); });

pm.test('only Friday now, overnight', () => { const s = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(s.openingHours).to.eql({ days: { fri: [{ opens: '22:00', closes: '02:00' }] } }); pm.expect(s.version).to.eql(2); });

request.description: F2.2: a flag, not intervals.

item.name: Open 24 hours: always open now, never changes

exec: pm.test('open now, no next change', () => { const s = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(s.openingHours).to.eql({ open24Hours: true }); pm.expect(s.isOpenNow).to.eql(true); pm.expect(s.nextChangeAt).to.eql(null); });

request.description: F5.4.7: only suppliers open at this moment, with correct totals and paging, combined with the other filters (F5.5).

exec: pm.test('our 24-hour supplier is open, whatever the time', () => pm.expect(page.items.some((s) => s.id === pm.environment.get('hoursSupplierId'))).to.be.true);
pm.test('every item is open now', () => pm.expect(page.items.every((s) => s.isOpenNow === true)).to.be.true);

item.name: Basic user asks to add a supplier with hours (201, Pending)

request.description: Hours are an ordinary supplier field, so a user can include them in a request. They are validated like an admin's (F2.4).

exec: pm.test('the proposed hours are recorded', () => pm.expect(r.values.openingHours.days.mon).to.eql([{ opens: '08:00', closes: '17:00' }]));

item.name: Admin approves it (200, hours go live)
The approved supplier has the proposed hours
Admin removes the hours with null (200)

request.description: null removes the schedule: the supplier has no fixed opening hours (F1.2.8).

item.name: No hours: isOpenNow is not applicable

exec: pm.test('all three are null (F2.5.1)', () => { const s = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(s.openingHours).to.eql(null); pm.expect(s.isOpenNow).to.eql(null); pm.expect(s.nextChangeAt).to.eql(null); });

item.name: Opening hours never change the status (F2.7)

request.description: Hours are informational only: they never change a supplier's status or block anything.

item.name: 7 Brands (after D2)
item.description: Brands group the outlets of one business (F3): list and manage brands, give suppliers an optional brand, filter and search by brand, a user proposing a brand in a request, renaming, removing and retiring (a supplier keeps a retired brand). Run folder 1 first (it saves the Food category and the PGP and COM3 building ids). Names are timestamped, so it can be re-run.

request.description: Any logged-in user can list the non-retired brands (F3.5), for example to fill a picker.

exec: pm.test('a list of {id, name}', () => { const list = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(list).to.be.an('array'); list.forEach((b) => pm.expect(Object.keys(b).sort()).to.eql(['id', 'name'])); });

request.description: F3.3. Names are 1-100 characters.
Case-insensitive among non-retired brands (F3.2); the same name with a different case is refused by the database's partial unique index.

item.name: A logo field is not accepted (400)

request.description: Logos are out of scope (images, F17), so only the name is accepted.

item.name: Admin creates the first outlet with the brand (201)

request.description: A supplier may have at most one brand (F3.4). The brand is optional (F1.2.10).

exec: pm.test('brand is {id, name}', () => pm.expect(s.brand).to.eql({ id: pm.environment.get('demoBrandId'), name: pm.environment.get('demoBrandName') }));

item.name: Second outlet of the same brand in another building (201)

request.description: Outlets of one brand are told apart by building, floor and display name (F3.4).

item.name: Unknown brand when creating a supplier (400)

exec: pm.test('brandId named', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().violations).to.eql([{ field: 'brandId', reason: 'brand does not exist' }]));

item.name: Filter the suppliers by brand (200, two outlets)

request.description: F5.4.6. Repeat the parameter to match several brands.

exec: pm.test('both outlets, each showing the brand', () => { pm.expect(page.total).to.eql(2); page.items.forEach((s) => pm.expect(s.brand.name).to.eql(pm.environment.get('demoBrandName'))); });

item.name: Brand and building combined (200, one outlet)

exec: pm.test('only the PGP outlet (F5.5)', () => { const page = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(page.total).to.eql(1); pm.expect(page.items[0].id).to.eql(pm.environment.get('brandOutlet2Id')); });

item.name: Search by the brand's name (200, both outlets)

request.description: The name search also matches the supplier's brand name (F5.4.1).

exec: pm.test('found through the brand name, though their own names differ (F5.4.1)', () => { const ids = pm.response.json().items.map((s) => s.id); pm.expect(ids).to.include.members([pm.environment.get('brandOutlet1Id'), pm.environment.get('brandOutlet2Id')]); });

item.name: Filter by a brand that does not exist (400)
Basic user asks to add a supplier with the brand (201, Pending)

request.description: A user can propose a brand from the existing ones. Only admins create brands.

item.name: The approved supplier has the brand

request.description: One rename updates every outlet, because suppliers reference the brand by id.

item.name: Every outlet shows the new name
Admin removes the brand from one outlet (200, version 2)

request.description: null removes the brand. Leaving the field out keeps it. Any change raises the version.

item.name: That outlet has no brand now

request.description: Suppliers keep it (F1.8), but it can no longer be chosen (F3.3.1).

item.name: Retired brand is no longer listed
Filtering by the retired brand returns nothing (200)

exec: pm.test('empty, though outlets keep it (F5.8.1)', () => { const page = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(page.total).to.eql(0); pm.expect(page.items).to.eql([]); });

item.name: An outlet still shows its retired brand (F1.8)
A retired brand cannot be newly chosen (400)

exec: pm.test('retired brand refused', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().violations).to.eql([{ field: 'brandId', reason: 'brand is retired and cannot be chosen' }]));

item.name: A retired brand cannot be renamed (409)
8 Safe retries: idempotency keys (after D2)
item.description: An Idempotency-Key header makes a create safe to repeat (F14.2): a repeat within 24 hours returns the original answer, a different request under the same key is refused, and only a success is stored. Run folder 1 first (it saves the Food category and the COM3 building id). Names and keys are generated per run, so it can be re-run.

item.name: Admin creates a category with an Idempotency-Key (201)

request.description: F14.2: the client chooses a unique key. Without the header nothing changes.

item.name: The same request again: the original answer (201, replayed)

request.description: A retry after a dropped connection: nothing is created twice, and the answer is the original one.

exec: pm.test('the same category, not a second one', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().id).to.eql(pm.environment.get('idemCategoryId')));

item.name: The same request with no key hits the duplicate rule (409)

request.description: What a retry looks like without a key: the client can't tell its first attempt worked.

item.name: The same key with a different body (422)

request.description: A key identifies one request. Nothing is done.

item.name: The same key on another endpoint (422)

request.description: The method and path are part of the request, so the same body on another endpoint is a different request.

item.name: Another user may use the same key (201)

request.description: Keys are per user, taken from the login token.

exec: pm.test('not a replay: keys belong to the user', () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.has('Idempotent-Replayed')).to.eql(false));

item.name: Retrying that request returns the same request (201, replayed)

request.description: Without the key this would be 409 DUPLICATE_REQUEST (an identical request is already pending).

exec: pm.test('exactly one request for that name', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().items.filter((r) => r.values.name === pm.environment.get('idemSupplierName')).length).to.eql(1));

item.name: Admin creates a supplier with a key (201, Location and ETag)

request.description: A direct admin create.

item.name: Retrying it replays the supplier, with its Location and ETag (201)
A failed attempt does not use up the key (400)

request.description: Only a success is stored.

item.name: The corrected request can reuse the key (201)

exec: pm.test('a fresh run, not a replay', () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.has('Idempotent-Replayed')).to.eql(false));

item.name: A key over 255 characters is refused (400)

request.description: The login is checked first.

item.name: 9 Audit log (after D2)
item.description: Every committed change to a supplier, request, category, brand or building is recorded (F14.4): who, what, the record before and after, the version, and when. Only admins can read the log, and nothing can change or delete an entry (F14.5). Run folder 1 first (it saves the Food category and the COM3 building id). Names are timestamped, so it can be re-run.

request.description: Every change like this writes an audit entry in the same transaction (F14.4).

item.name: Admin reads the entry: who, what, where (200)

request.description: Admin only. Newest first.

exec: pm.test('the actor is the admin from the token', () => pm.expect(page.items[0].actorId).to.eql(pm.environment.get('auditAdminSub')));

pm.test('a creation has no before, and the new values after', () => { pm.expect(page.items[0].before).to.eql(null); pm.expect(page.items[0].after.name).to.eql(pm.environment.get('auditCategoryName')); });

item.name: Admin renames it, then reads the log: before and after (200)
The rename is recorded with the old and new name

exec: pm.test('newest first: renamed, then created', () => pm.expect(items.map((e) => e.action)).to.eql(['category.renamed', 'category.created']));

item.name: A refused change leaves no entry: the total before

request.description: Nothing is created, so nothing is recorded.

exec: pm.test('no entry for the refused change', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().total).to.eql(pm.environment.get('auditCreatedTotal')));

item.name: The supplier's entries: created, then updated with before and after
Basic user asks for a supplier (201, Pending)
The request's entries: submitted by the user, approved by the admin

exec: pm.test('by the admin, and by a different user than the submission', () => { pm.expect(items[0].actorId).to.eql(pm.environment.get('auditAdminSub')); pm.expect(items[1].actorId).to.not.eql(items[0].actorId); });

item.name: The supplier the approval created is attributed to the admin

exec: pm.test('supplier.created by the approving admin, in the same transaction', () => { pm.expect(items.length).to.eql(1); pm.expect(items[0].action).to.eql('supplier.created'); pm.expect(items[0].actorId).to.eql(pm.environment.get('auditAdminSub')); });

item.name: Filter by the admin: every entry is theirs

exec: pm.test('only that actor', () => { const page = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(page.items.length).to.be.above(0); pm.expect(page.items.every((e) => e.actorId === pm.environment.get('auditAdminSub'))).to.be.true; });

item.name: A basic user cannot read the log (403)
There is no way to delete an entry (404)

request.description: The log is append-only (F14.5): no route changes it, and the database refuses UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE as well.
